title: Dependency escrow lanes and release timeboxing for multi-team cutovers
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a pragmatic playbook for 'dependency escrow lanes' and 'release timeboxing' to reduce cross-team cutover risk for high-impact roadmap items. The goal is to provide deterministic handoffs between Eng, Design, Security, and Infra teams so that multi-team releases hit SLAs and have observable rollback/mitigation windows.

Why this is needed:
- We continue to see late-stage blockers in multi-team cutovers (design polish, security gating, infra config).
- Lack of clear escrow lanes creates ambiguous ownership when a downstream team is blocked.
- Timeboxing windows with explicit guardrails reduces release friction and gives product owners deterministic go/no-go decisions.

Scope:
- Define three escrow lanes (Green: no blocker, Amber: mitigatable blocker, Red: blocking with escalation path).
- Timebox cutover windows per release (Canary, Broad, Cutover) with minimum telemetry gating for each stage.
- Standard handoff artifacts and templates (deployment checklist, design QA signoff, security checklist, infra runbook).
- Automation hooks for Console dashboards (deployment status, dependency health) and Slack escalation channels.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement per-model runtime changes. It is a process + templates + light automation integration (dashboard & alerts). Full runtime changes will follow as separate ENG tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Escrow lane definitions (Green/Amber/Red) documented in Confluence and linked in the release template
Timeboxing templates added to the release checklist with explicit durations for Canary/Broad/Cutover windows
Handoff artifact checklist (design QA link, security signoff, infra config snapshot) exists and is used by at least two pilot releases
Console dashboard shows dependency health and stage gating for pilot releases
Escalation playbook executed in a simulated runway drill with on-call participants and postmortem notes
plan_steps: Week 1: Draft escrow lane definitions and timebox defaults; review with Eng, Design, Security, Infra
Week 2: Create release checklist templates and Confluence pages; build Slack escalation channels and runbook
Week 3: Implement lightweight Console dashboard widgets (status + dependency counts) with metrics owner
Week 4: Run two pilot cutovers (one Hosted API feature, one Dedicated capacity change); collect feedback
Week 5: Iterate on templates and onboard broader teams; finalize playbook and ship as best-practice doc
risks: Teams may treat escrow lanes as bureaucratic and not adopt without leadership enforcement
Console telemetry gaps could block automated gating; will require infra instrumentation work
Timeboxes may be too rigid for certain emergent security work and need explicit exemption flow
stakeholders: Sana Patel (Design) - UX handoff and QA
decisions: Use three-lane escrow model (Green/Amber/Red) instead of per-team statuses to simplify cross-team communication
Default Canary window = 2 hours, Broad = 6 hours, Cutover = 24 hours (editable per-release)
Security exemptions require documented risk acceptance and Ops aware of rollback plan
Pilot releases will include both a Hosted API feature and a Dedicated infra change to validate patterns
